title: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say
key_facts: TechCrunch reported on 5 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the company, that AI chip start-up Etched is being offered funding at valuations of $40 billion and above.
Offers range from $40 billion from top-tier investors to $50 billion from lesser-known backers, one person said; the talks are early, terms may change and Etched declined to comment.
Etched raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation in September 2026, led by Jane Street, and $300 million at $10.3 billion in July, led by Sequoia.
If it raises as much as its last round, the person said, Etched could have as much as 3.5 years of runway.
Etched builds full AI hardware systems on its own chips and says they process more tokens faster and at a lower cost than Nvidia's, which is the company's own claim.
Etched said in July it had $1 billion in customer orders, including from Jane Street, which also took delivery of an early system; its test chip was made at a TSMC factory this summer.
About 15% of its roughly 400 staff previously worked at Nvidia (Wall Street Journal, cited by TechCrunch); it runs a 10-megawatt data center in Silicon Valley and has a facility in Taiwan.
quote_evidence: Etched is reviewing incoming bids that range from $40 billion from top-tier investors to $50 billion from lesser-known backers, one person said.
These fundraising talks are early, so terms of any deal, should one happen, may change.
The company claims its chips can process more tokens faster and at a lower cost than Nvidia’s.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are reportedly offering double or more of Etched's value of a few months ago, a sign of appetite for challengers to Nvidia's chips.
notes: Full TechCrunch article read. The article says it has been only 'a couple of months' since the $700 million round and dates that round to September 2026. The valuations are offers, not a closed deal.
